articles.title: Why are my monstera leaves turning yellow?
articles.body: Yellowing usually means overwatering. Let the top two inches of soil dry out before watering again.

articles.title: Keeping ferns from crisping up
articles.body: Ferns want humidity above 50%. Group plants together or use a pebble tray.

articles.title: Fungus gnats in the soil
articles.body: Gnats breed in wet soil. Let the top layer dry out fully, add a layer of grit, and use yellow sticky traps. Do not water more.

articles.title: Fine webbing and speckled leaves: spider mites
articles.body: Shower the plant, wipe both sides of every leaf, raise humidity and repeat weekly for three weeks.

articles.title: A drooping pothos
articles.body: Drooping is thirst or cold. Check the soil: dry means water deeply; wet means it is too cold or the roots are rotting.

articles.title: When to repot
articles.body: Repot in spring when roots circle the pot. Go up one size only; a pot that is too big holds water and rots roots.

articles.title: Brown edges on a calathea
articles.body: Tap water minerals and dry air. Use rainwater or filtered water and keep humidity up.

articles.title: Soft, mushy succulent
articles.body: Rot from overwatering. Stop watering, remove soft leaves, let it dry for a week; water only when the soil is bone dry.

articles.title: Peace lily wilting
articles.body: It wilts when thirsty and recovers within hours of a drink. If it does not recover, the roots are waterlogged.

articles.title: Orchid after the flowers drop
articles.body: Cut the spike above the second node, keep watering weekly, and it reflowers in a few months.

articles.title: Snake plant light and water
articles.body: Any light, water every three to four weeks. Most snake plants die from kindness.

articles.title: White fluff in the leaf joints: mealybugs
articles.body: Dab each one with a cotton bud in rubbing alcohol, then spray with insecticidal soap weekly.

articles.title: A plant that arrived damaged
articles.body: Photograph it in the box within 48 hours and message us; we replace or refund, your choice.

articles.title: Pausing or skipping a monthly box
articles.body: Skip a month from Account > Subscription up to five days before the dispatch date.

articles.title: Cancelling the monthly box
articles.body: Cancel any time from Account > Subscription; it stops after the box already paid for.

articles.title: The wrong plant was sent
articles.body: Keep it; send a photo and we dispatch the right one at no charge.

articles.title: Leggy, stretched growth
articles.body: Not enough light. Move closer to a window and turn the pot weekly; prune back to a node.

articles.title: Rescuing a plant with root rot
articles.body: Unpot, cut away brown mushy roots, repot in fresh dry mix, and do not water for a week.

articles.title: Watering in winter
articles.body: Halve the watering from November to February; growth slows and wet soil goes cold.

articles.title: Plants that are safe around cats and dogs
articles.body: Spider plant, calathea, peperomia, Boston fern and areca palm are safe. Lilies, pothos and monstera are not.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: There are tiny flies all over the soil of my plants, loads of them.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Gnats breed in wet soil. Let the top layer dry out fully, add a layer of grit, and use yellow sticky traps. Do not water more. (From: Fungus gnats in the soil)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: That makes sense, thank you.

messages.body: Should I water less now it is cold?

messages.body: Halve the watering from November to February; growth slows and wet soil goes cold. (From: Watering in winter)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Great, cheers.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: The leaves on my monstera are going yellow from the bottom up.

messages.body: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of thirst. Water more often and add a feed every week. (From: Why are my monstera leaves turning yellow?)

messages.body: No, I asked about something else.

messages.body: Let me get someone from the nursery to look at this with you.

messages.body: Not enough light. Move closer to a window and turn the pot weekly; prune back to a node. (From: Leggy, stretched growth)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: That does not match what is happening at all.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Let me know how it goes after a week.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: The peace lily has flopped right over.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: It wilts when thirsty and recovers within hours of a drink. If it does not recover, the roots are waterlogged. (From: Peace lily wilting)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Roots are coming out of the bottom of the pot, do I repot now?

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Repot in spring when roots circle the pot. Go up one size only; a pot that is too big holds water and rots roots. (From: When to repot)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Which of your plants are safe with a cat?

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Spider plant, calathea, peperomia, Boston fern and areca palm are safe. Lilies, pothos and monstera are not. (From: Plants that are safe around cats and dogs)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: That makes sense, thank you.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: I am away next month, can I skip the box?

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: I can help with that. Skip a month from Account > Subscription up to five days before the dispatch date. (From: Pausing or skipping a monthly box)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Is Rose around?

messages.author: SYSTEM
messages.body: Handed to Rose Okafor

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Rose from the nursery here. Cancelled from next month as asked; the box already paid for still comes.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Great, cheers.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: My pothos has gone completely limp overnight.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Drooping is thirst or cold. Check the soil: dry means water deeply; wet means it is too cold or the roots are rotting. (From: A drooping pothos)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: My echeveria has gone soft and see-through at the bottom.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Rot from overwatering. Stop watering, remove soft leaves, let it dry for a week; water only when the soil is bone dry. (From: Soft, mushy succulent)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Great, cheers.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: I think the roots have rotted, the soil smells.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Cut the spike above the second node, keep watering weekly, and it reflowers in a few months. (From: Orchid after the flowers drop)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: That does not match what is happening at all.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Let me know how it goes after a week.

messages.author: CUSTOMER

messages.author: STAFF

messages.author: CUSTOMER

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: My Boston fern is crisping at the tips even though I water it.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Ferns want humidity above 50%. Group plants together or use a pebble tray. (From: Keeping ferns from crisping up)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: The edges of my calathea leaves are brown and crispy.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Tap water minerals and dry air. Use rainwater or filtered water and keep humidity up. (From: Brown edges on a calathea)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: The leaves on my monstera are going yellow from the bottom up.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Yellowing usually means overwatering. Let the top two inches of soil dry out before watering again. (From: Why are my monstera leaves turning yellow?)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: No, I asked about something else.

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Let me know how it goes after a week.

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Should I water less now it is cold?

messages.author: STAFF
messages.body: Halve the watering from November to February; growth slows and wet soil goes cold. (From: Watering in winter)

messages.author: CUSTOMER
messages.body: Will do, thanks!
